HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
Policy wording "WD-2026" - Theft, Break-in and Scheduled Articles Edition

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with the
Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods, percentages and endorsements shown in square brackets or
marked as optional are those stated in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

This insurance protects the policyholder against the financial consequences of
the loss of, or physical damage to, insured movable property, and against the
damage done to the insured premises in the course of an entry by force. The
perils that can be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions -
among them theft and break-in, fire, escape of water and the natural hazards.
Which of the insurable perils are actually covered, and which endorsements apply,
is agreed between insurer and policyholder and recorded in the schedule.

Where insured property is taken, destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies
the value of that property, or the cost of putting it back, on the basis set out
in Part 6 and within the sums insured and sub-limits agreed. A limited and
exhaustively listed range of consequential expenses is also carried, within the
limits agreed for each head.

Three lines run through the whole of this wording. The first divides the property
that was taken or damaged from everything else. The second divides making good
that loss from putting the household generally back in order. The third divides
the indemnity itself from the effort of claiming it: what the policyholder spends
in evidencing, reporting and presenting a claim is the policyholder's own, not a
head of loss.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage or an item of property for which no cover
exists. Exclusions delimit what has been promised and keep the cover calculable.

Affected item - an item of insured property which was taken, destroyed, damaged
or lost in the insured event, and which is identified and evidenced as such in
the itemisation under 7.1.10.

Physical damage - a change in the substance, structure or working condition of
property. Soiling, marking, disarrangement and comparable traces which leave the
substance intact are not physical damage (3.1.7).

Scheduled article - an individual item listed in the scheduled-articles
endorsement with a value agreed between the parties. A scheduled article is
indemnified at that agreed value in place of any per-item or aggregate sub-limit
which would otherwise apply to its class.

Sub-limit - a monetary ceiling that applies within the sum insured to a defined
class of property or to a defined head of cost. Where a sub-limit applies, the
class or head is indemnified only up to that ceiling; the excess is borne by the
policyholder. Where the loss on that class or head remains below the ceiling, the
sub-limit does not reduce the indemnity.

Ancillary charge - any charge raised alongside the value of the affected items or
the itemised labour and materials: call-out and travel, carriage and dispatch,
fitting, administration, handling, reporting and comparable items.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before, during
and after an insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is taken, destroyed or damaged by,
or lost as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) THEFT of insured property from the insured premises, and the damage done to
      insured property in the course of a theft or an attempted theft;

  (b) BREAK-IN DAMAGE to the insured premises, to their fittings and to their
      locking and closing equipment;

  (c) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot;

  (d) ESCAPE OF WATER;

  (e) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (e1) storm and hail;
        (e2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the groups (a), (b), (c), (d) and (e1) can be taken separately. The
further natural hazards under (e2) can only be taken in combination with one or
more of the other groups.

2.3 Theft defined

2.3.1 What the peril is
Theft is the taking of insured property from the insured premises against the
policyholder's will and with the intention of keeping it, where the perpetrator
gained access by an act falling within 2.4. Covered under this heading are the
loss of the items taken and the physical damage done to insured property in the
course of the taking or the attempt.

2.3.2 Damage excluded within this peril
Not covered:
  (a) property mislaid, misplaced, forgotten or left behind, and a shortfall
      established only on a later review of possessions and not attributable to
      an identified event;
  (b) property surrendered voluntarily, including on a deception or a false
      pretext;
  (c) property taken by a person who lives in the insured premises, who is
      employed in the household, or to whom access was entrusted;
  (d) an item whose presence in the household at the time of the event, or whose
      loss in that event, is not evidenced under 7.1.10.

2.4 Break-in defined

2.4.1 A break-in is present where a person breaks into, forces open, breaks out
of, or enters by comparable means the insured premises, a part of them, or a
locked receptacle within them, or where a person uses a key or code obtained
through such an act or by force against a person.

2.4.2 The indemnity under 2.1(b) comprises the making good of the affected fabric
and fittings: doors and door leaves, frames, thresholds and surrounds; windows,
shutters and their frames; locks, cylinders, escutcheons, handles, hinges, bolts
and comparable hardware; the associated glazing; and the affected surfaces and
finishes. Where a lock or locking system has been damaged, opened or compromised,
the indemnity comprises its replacement and, where the compromised element forms
part of a system, the re-keying or replacement of the further elements of that
system necessary to restore its security.

2.4.3 Securing the premises provisionally until the permanent repair can be
carried out is covered under 5.2.2.

2.4.4 Not covered under this heading is the strengthening of the security of the
premises beyond the standard in place immediately before the event, and the
fitting of additional locking, closing, monitoring or alarm equipment (7.1.9).

2.5 Fire group, escape of water and natural hazards

2.5.1 The fire group covers fire - a combustion that has started without a hearth
intended for it, or that has escaped such a hearth, and that is capable of
spreading under its own power - together with lightning strike, overvoltage
caused by lightning, explosion, deflagration, implosion, aircraft impact, vehicle
impact, scorching, and smoke and soot. Damage from the gradual action of smoke or
soot is not covered.

2.5.2 Escaping water means water that has emerged contrary to its intended
purpose from the water, heating, air-conditioning, extinguishing or comparable
installations of the building in which the insured property is located.

2.5.3 Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale
threshold on the recognised scale of wind strength; hail means solid
precipitation in the form of grains of ice. The further natural hazards are
flood, backing-up of water, earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load,
avalanche and volcanic eruption, each as customarily defined.

2.5.4 Not covered within these groups is damage caused by storm surge; by the
penetration of precipitation or dirt through openings that were not properly
closed; by groundwater save where it emerged at the surface as a result of
precipitation or overflow; by earthquake within the fire group; and by drought or
desiccation.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered, irrespective of any
contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.4 Liability risks
Claims of third parties against the policyholder, and any outlay directed at
covering, assessing, administering or settling such claims, are not the subject
of this contract.

3.1.5 Preparation, reporting and substantiation of the claim
Establishing, evidencing, reporting and presenting the claim is a matter for the
policyholder at its own expense. Outlay directed at the cause, the extent or the
substantiation of the loss, or at bringing the claim to the insurer or to a
public authority, is not an indemnifiable head of loss under this contract.

This applies in particular to journeys, travel, mileage, fares and vehicle costs
incurred by the policyholder or by a member of the household in reporting the
event or in dealing with the claim; to the time, effort and inconvenience of
listing the property lost, compiling the supporting documents, completing the
forms and corresponding with the insurer or with any other body, whether valued
at an hourly rate, at a daily rate, as lost earnings or as a lump sum; and to
charges for obtaining, copying, certifying, translating or forwarding documents
for the purposes of the claim. It applies whether the outlay is claimed by the
policyholder or billed by a third party engaged for the purpose.

Nothing in this clause reduces the policyholder's own duty of substantiation
under 7.1.10, and nothing in it affects the allocation of the costs of an expert
determination under Part 8.

3.1.6 Service, assistance and administration arrangements
Outlay arising from a service, assistance, support, representation, handling or
comparable arrangement, and any charge for opening, registering, administering or
processing a claim file, is not indemnifiable.

3.1.7 Soiling, traces and cleaning
Soiling, marking, staining of a superficial kind, footprints, deposits,
disarrangement and comparable traces left on the insured premises or on insured
property, where the substance itself remains intact, are not physical damage and
are not an insured loss. The cleaning, washing, wiping, sweeping, shampooing,
tidying and restoration of order that removes such traces is an act of upkeep and
is not indemnifiable, whoever performs it, at whatever point after the event, and
whether it is billed by the trade that also carries out indemnifiable work.

Where the substance was itself damaged - torn, broken, cut, scorched, saturated,
gouged or otherwise altered - the making good of that damage falls under 7.1, and
the removal of the residues and debris generated by the covered making-good works
falls under 5.2.5.

3.1.8 Upkeep, improvement and precautionary measures
Outlay directed at the servicing, maintenance, cleaning, general condition,
modernisation or improvement of property, and the renewal of an item on which no
damage from the insured event has been established, is not indemnifiable, even
where the measure is taken as a precaution or on a recommendation.

3.1.9 Consequential disruption
The consequences an insured event has for the policyholder's arrangements are not
insured. Not indemnifiable in particular are replacement, additional or
rearranged travel and transport; additional or extended accommodation; meals and
subsistence; missed or forfeited bookings; and time, inconvenience, loss of use
and loss of earnings. The heads expressly listed in 5.1 remain unaffected within
their own preconditions and limits.

3.2 Exclusions within the theft and break-in perils

See 2.3.2 and 2.4.4.

3.3 Exclusions within the remaining perils

See 2.5.4.

3.4 Outlay that is not an indemnity for property

Outlay that does not represent the value of an affected item, the cost of making
good physical damage to an affected item or to the insured premises, or a head
expressly listed in Part 5, is not indemnified. The delimitation is governed by
7.1.5 to 7.1.10.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises the movable items belonging to the household of the
policyholder and serving its private use, insofar as the policyholder owns them
or bears the risk for them, together with the classes of property described in
4.2 within the sub-limits stated in the schedule, and - for the peril under
2.1(b) - the fabric, fittings and locking equipment of the insured premises
insofar as the policyholder bears the risk for them.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 General household effects
Movable items of ordinary household use, including clothing, footwear, garments
of every season and weight, luggage, and the ordinary personal effects of the
occupants. This class carries no sub-limit of its own; it is indemnified up to
the sum insured stated in the schedule.

4.2.2 Valuables
Items of jewellery, adornment worked from precious metals or set with precious or
semi-precious stones, timepieces, loose precious metals and stones, collections
and comparable items of concentrated value form a single class of property.
Indemnity for this class is subject to the valuables sub-limit stated in the
schedule, applied per item and, where more than one such item is affected, in the
aggregate per insured event.

An item of this class is not removed from it by everyday or habitual use, and an
item is not brought into it by price alone. Where several modest items of the
class are affected and their aggregate value remains below the ceiling, the
sub-limit does not reduce the indemnity (6.3).

4.2.3 Scheduled articles
An individual item listed in the scheduled-articles endorsement with a value
agreed between the parties is indemnified at that agreed value. The per-item and
aggregate sub-limits of its class do not apply to it, and its value does not
consume the aggregate available to the unscheduled items of that class.

Where an item of a class carrying a sub-limit is not listed in that endorsement,
the sub-limit applies to it whatever its actual value and whatever evidence of a
higher value is produced.

4.2.4 Means of payment
Cash, cash equivalents and comparable means of payment form a single class,
subject to the sub-limit stated in the schedule and applied in the aggregate per
insured event.

4.2.5 Allocation to a class
Each affected item is allocated to exactly one class under 4.2.1, 4.2.2 or 4.2.4
according to its nature, subject to 4.2.3.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) property used predominantly for a trade, business or profession;
  (b) motor vehicles requiring registration, watercraft and aircraft, and their
      parts and accessories;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs, and the restoration, migration or
      re-registration of software, media content, user accounts and comparable
      intangible items;
  (d) documents, entitlements and credit balances as such, and the cost of their
      cancellation, blocking, re-issue or re-registration;
  (e) property acquired on the occasion of the loss which does not replace an
      affected item of the same kind and intended purpose;
  (f) an item claimed without the evidence required under 7.1.10.

4.4 Optionally insurable

Individual items may be listed at an agreed value in the scheduled-articles
endorsement, and classes of property may be insured at raised sub-limits, where
this is agreed and recorded in the schedule.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the dwelling stated in the schedule together with the
ancillary rooms and stores belonging to it.

4.6 Several persons entitled

Where several persons are entitled under this contract, the insurer may render
its benefit to any one of them with effect for all.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. Deductibles can be agreed individually and may
differ from one insured peril and one insured benefit to another. Each is set out
in the schedule. The deductible is applied once per insured event to the covered
settlement, irrespective of the number of items, classes, trades or invoices
involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) the cost of averting or mitigating the loss;
  (b) the cost of provisionally securing and closing the insured premises after a
      break-in, and of making them safe;
  (c) the cost of changing the locks of the insured premises where their keys
      were taken in an insured event;
  (d) the cost of moving and protecting insured property;
  (e) the cost of removing and disposing of destroyed insured property and of the
      material taken out in the course of the covered works;
  (f) hotel costs where the insured premises have become uninhabitable through
      physical damage caused by an insured peril.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it. This
list is exhaustive. A head of cost that does not fall within it, and that is not a
repair cost within the meaning of 7.1.7, is not insured, however closely it is
connected with the insured event and however reasonably it was incurred.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Averting and mitigating the loss
Costs of measures taken during or immediately after the insured event to prevent
the loss from occurring or from increasing, capped at [amount] per insured event.

5.2.2 Provisional securing of the premises
Costs of the measures taken during or immediately after a break-in to close,
board, cover, bar, provisionally lock or otherwise secure the point of entry and
the premises, and to make them safe, so that the premises can be left until the
permanent repair is carried out. These measures are covered whether they are
carried out at once, outside normal working hours, at a call-out rate, or on a
later occasion, and whether by the trade that afterwards performs the permanent
repair or by another. Indemnity is capped at [amount] per insured event.

5.2.3 Change of locks
Costs of replacing the locks of the insured premises where their keys were taken
in an insured event, capped at [amount] per insured event.

5.2.4 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting property, where those measures
serve to secure or reinstate insured property.

5.2.5 Removal and disposal
Costs of removing and disposing of destroyed insured property and of the material
taken out in the course of the covered making-good works, including the residues
and debris those works generate. This head does not extend to the cleaning
described in 3.1.7.

5.2.6 Hotel costs
Costs of accommodation where the insured premises have become uninhabitable
through physical damage caused by an insured peril and confining oneself to a
habitable part cannot reasonably be expected, reimbursed only where indemnity
cannot be claimed under another insurance contract, up to [amount] per day for a
maximum of [number] days.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. It is
determined separately for each class of property under 4.2, and for a scheduled
article by the value agreed for it.

6.2 Replacement value

6.2.1 What is insured is the amount that would have to be spent to procure
property of the same kind and quality in new condition at the time of the insured
event. No deduction is made for the age of an item, for the use made of it, or
for the ordinary wear of an item in serviceable condition.

6.2.2 By way of exception, for items whose current value has fallen to a
substantial extent below the replacement value - in particular through advanced
age, heavy wear, technical obsolescence or prolonged disuse - the current value
applies in place of the replacement value. Recent acquisition, brief use or
seasonal use does not bring an item within this exception, and an item that had
been little used before the event is indemnified under 6.2.1 without abatement.

6.2.3 For a scheduled article, the agreed value applies (4.2.3).

6.2.4 For the means of payment, the nominal value applies.

6.3 Relationship between basis of cover and sub-limits

The basis of cover under 6.2 does not displace a sub-limit. Where a class of
property carries a sub-limit, the sub-limit determines the ceiling of the
indemnity for that class even where the insurable value demonstrably exceeds it,
and the balance is borne by the policyholder. Conversely, a sub-limit is a
ceiling and not a fixed benefit: where the indemnifiable loss on that class is
lower, the indemnity is the loss, and where the class carries no sub-limit the
indemnifiable loss is paid within the sum insured.

6.4 Permanently devalued property

For property that can no longer be used for its purpose, only the achievable sale
price is insured.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the sum insured, the area and type of
the insured premises, the sub-limits and endorsements agreed, the deductible
agreed, the security arrangements agreed, other agreed features material to the
premium calculation, and the adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted, the premium changes accordingly. The adjustment factor
changes with effect from 1 January of each year in line with the movement of the
relevant published price indices, weighted as agreed and rounded to two decimal
places.

6.7 Subsequent change in a premium-rating feature

Where a rating circumstance subsequently changes and a higher premium results,
the insurer may demand the higher premium from the point at which the change is
notified. Where such a circumstance ceases to apply and a lower premium results,
the insurer must reduce the premium from the point at which it becomes aware of
that.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for taken, destroyed or lost items - the insurable value under Part 6 at
      the time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged items - the necessary repair costs at the time of the insured
      event, together with any diminution in value the repair does not offset,
      capped at the insurable value of the item;
  (c) for the fabric, fittings and locking equipment of the insured premises -
      the necessary repair costs, including the replacement components and
      hardware, their fitting into the premises, the labour hours of every grade
      employed on that work, and the sundry materials consumed by it;
  (d) for the means of payment - the nominal value.

Where the property concerned belongs to a class carrying a sub-limit, the
indemnity under (a) or (b) is confined to that sub-limit, save for a scheduled
article (4.2.3).

7.1.2 Where property that was taken is recovered, the policyholder must notify
the insurer without delay. Property recovered before the indemnity is paid is
treated as damaged property; property recovered afterwards is either surrendered
to the insurer or retained against repayment.

7.1.3 Price increases occurring between the insured event and the replacement are
indemnified where the replacement is secured within [number] months.

7.1.4 The achievable sale price of remains is set off in calculating the
indemnity.

7.1.5 Extent of the indemnity
Indemnity is confined to the affected items and to the affected parts of the
insured premises. Property supplied for, and work carried out on, an item or a
part that was not itself affected is not covered, even where it is done so that
affected and unaffected items correspond in appearance or equipment; for reasons
of convenience or economy; as a precaution against a future event; at the same
time as covered work or in the course of it; or by the same trade as the covered
work and invoiced together with it.

7.1.6 Sets and matched items
Where one item of a set, suite, pair or collection was affected, indemnity is
confined to that item and does not extend to the remaining, unaffected items,
whatever the loss of uniformity or completeness. Where the affected element forms
part of a locking or closing system whose security depends on the integrity of
the whole, 2.4.2 applies.

7.1.7 What the repair cost comprises
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) and (c) include the removal,
dismantling and disposal of the damaged parts; replacement components and
hardware of a type, quality, grade and specification corresponding to those in
place immediately before the insured event; their fitting, mounting, adjustment
and functional testing; the labour hours needed for that work at every grade of
personnel employed on it, at the rates customary in the trade; the small parts,
fixings and comparable sundry materials consumed by it; and one attendance at the
insured premises by each trade performing indemnifiable work, in addition to any
attendance forming part of a measure under 5.2.2.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not an indemnity for property
The following are not indemnified, however they may be described, bundled or
invoiced, by whichever party they are raised, and irrespective of whether they
appear on an invoice or settlement statement that also contains an indemnifiable
element:

  (a) the cleaning, washing, wiping, tidying and restoration of order described in
      3.1.7, and every measure directed at the general condition, cleanliness,
      upkeep, modernisation or improvement of property (3.1.8);

  (b) the renewal of an item or a part on which no damage from the insured event
      has been established, and every measure directed at property outside Part 4;

  (c) the improvement element where a replacement of a higher grade, superior
      material, larger size or premium range is chosen; indemnity for that item is
      limited to the cost of an equivalent standard-grade replacement
      corresponding to what was in place before the loss, and the difference is
      borne by the policyholder (7.1.9);

  (d) the strengthening of the security of the premises beyond the standard in
      place immediately before the event (2.4.4);

  (e) journeys, mileage, fares, time, effort and comparable outlay of the
      policyholder or of a member of the household in reporting the event or in
      compiling, evidencing and presenting the claim, however quantified (3.1.5);

  (f) charges of the kind described in 3.1.4, 3.1.6 and 3.1.9, including
      administrative, handling, order-processing, claim-processing and file-opening
      charges levied in addition to the itemised benefit;

  (g) carriage, freight, delivery, dispatch, packaging, postage and comparable
      charges for bringing replacement property to the insured premises;

  (h) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of the
      same insured event, whether by one party or across several; only the first
      such charge is indemnified.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
The indemnity proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade, size, material
and specification of the affected item immediately before the insured event.
Where a higher specification, a superior material, a premium range or a
better-known maker is chosen instead, indemnity is limited to the cost of an
equivalent standard-grade replacement corresponding to what was in place before
the loss; the difference is borne by the policyholder. Where the item held before
the loss is no longer obtainable, the nearest currently available equivalent of
the same grade sets the ceiling; an unavoidable difference is not treated as an
improvement, a chosen one is.

7.1.10 Itemisation, evidence and apportionment
The policyholder itemises each affected item - its description, its approximate
age or date of acquisition, its value, and the class to which it belongs - and
supports the itemisation, for each item, by such evidence of its existence,
ownership and value as can reasonably be expected: a receipt, an invoice, a bank
or card record, a photograph, a valuation, a certificate, a manufacturer's or
retailer's record, a guarantee document, a listing in the scheduled-articles
endorsement, or comparable material.

Where no such evidence is produced for an item, that item is not indemnified. The
insurer does not infer the existence, the ownership or the value of an
unevidenced item from the fact that other items in the same claim are evidenced,
from the plausibility of its presence in the household, or from the circumstances
of the event.

Where an invoice or settlement line bundles indemnifiable and non-indemnifiable
elements and the elements can be identified and valued from the documents, the
line is apportioned. Where they cannot be separated, the line is assessed by its
predominant stated purpose; where the predominant purpose is not indemnifiable,
the line is not indemnified. Where a line bundles several affected items of one
class carrying a sub-limit, that sub-limit is applied to the line as a whole.

Labour hours, sundry materials, fitting charges and attendance charges are
allocated to the work they served; where that work is not indemnifiable, they are
not indemnifiable either.

7.2 Devalued property

Insofar as property can no longer be used for its purpose, it is indemnified at
the achievable sale price.

7.3 Sum insured lower or higher than the insurable value

Where the sum insured is lower than the insurable value at the time of the insured
event, the indemnity is reduced in the proportion the sum insured bears to the
insurable value, insofar as this is agreed. Where the sum insured is higher, the
insurer is not obliged to compensate more than the loss actually incurred.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they were
actually incurred, and the indemnity limits agreed for each head are applied.

7.5 Order of application

The indemnity is determined in the following order: the indemnifiable loss is
established item by item under 7.1, with 7.1.9 applied to each; the items are
allocated to their classes, scheduled articles being taken separately; the class
sub-limits under Part 4 are then applied; the insured costs under Part 5 are added
within their own limits; and the deductible under 7.8 is deducted once from the
resulting amount.

7.6 Replacement element of the indemnity

Where the basis of cover is the replacement value, the policyholder acquires a
claim to that part of the indemnity which exceeds the current value only where it
demonstrates that it has secured the replacement of property of the same kind and
intended purpose within the period under 7.1.3.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred on the occasion of the replacement or repair, and not where the
policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed, once per insured
event.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim as
to its basis and its amount. One month after notifying the loss, the policyholder
may claim as an interim payment the amount that is, on the prevailing assessment,
payable as a minimum.

7.10 Repayment

The policyholder must repay indemnity paid on the replacement basis where, through
its own fault, the property was not replaced within a reasonable period, and must
repay indemnity for property subsequently recovered and retained.

7.11 Interest

The indemnity bears interest from the notification of the loss, save where paid
within one month. The rate is [number] percentage point(s) below the applicable
statutory base rate, but at least [percentage] and at most [percentage] per year.

7.12 Suspension of time limits

Any period during which the indemnity cannot be determined or paid owing to the
fault of the policyholder is left out of account.

7.13 Deferral of payment

The insurer may defer payment for as long as there is doubt as to the
policyholder's entitlement to receive payment, or official or criminal proceedings
arising out of this insured event are pending.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the
amount of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer and
policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly, and may agree to extend it
to further determinations relating to the insured event.

8.2 Each party nominates one expert in text form. Where a party fails to nominate
within two weeks of a request, the requesting party may have the expert appointed
by the court with local jurisdiction for the loss location. Before beginning their
determinations, the two experts nominate a third expert as umpire.

8.3 The experts' findings must state a schedule of the taken, destroyed and damaged
insured property with the corresponding insurable values; the repair and
replacement costs; the residual values; and the insured costs. Where a class of
property carries a sub-limit, the findings state the loss for that class
separately, and state scheduled articles separately again, so that the limits can
be applied. Where an item's existence, ownership or value is disputed, the findings
state on what evidence the answer rests.

8.4 Each expert transmits its findings to both parties simultaneously. Where the
findings diverge, the umpire decides the points that remain in dispute within the
limits set by the experts' findings. The findings are binding unless they
manifestly deviate substantially from the true state of affairs.

8.5 Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert; the costs of the umpire are borne in equal shares. A report, valuation or
other document obtained by one party outside this procedure remains that party's
own cost (3.1.5).

8.6 The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Duties before an insured event

9.1.1 The insured premises must be kept secured in the customary manner; doors and
windows must be closed and locked when the premises are left unattended, and the
agreed locking and closing equipment must be kept operational.

9.1.2 Items of the class under 4.2.2, and scheduled articles, must be kept in the
manner agreed in the schedule when not in use.

9.1.3 The policyholder should keep the receipts, valuations, photographs and
comparable records of the property insured, so that the itemisation under 7.1.10
can be supported after a loss. Keeping them is a matter for the policyholder at its
own expense (3.1.5).

9.2 Duties after an insured event

9.2.1 The policyholder must avert and mitigate the loss so far as can reasonably be
expected, secure the premises without delay, and follow the insurer's instructions
where these can be obtained.

9.2.2 The policyholder must report a theft or break-in without delay to the
competent public authority, notify the insurer without delay, and keep the affected
state unchanged until released.

9.2.3 The policyholder must provide the itemisation and the supporting evidence
under 7.1.10 and give the insurer any information required to assess the claim. The
expense of doing so is borne by the policyholder (3.1.5).

9.3 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of these duties, and subject to the conditions
set out in the general contract provisions, the insurer is entitled to terminate
the contract and may be wholly or partly released from liability.

9.4 Increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification may exist in particular where the
insured premises are left unoccupied for a prolonged period, where the agreed
security or locking arrangements are altered or cease to be operational, or where
the composition or value of a class of property under 4.2 changes materially. The
consequences are governed by the general contract provisions.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION AND CHANGE OF CIRCUMSTANCES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation after an insured event

After an insured event for which the insurer has rendered a benefit, or has
declined to do so, each party may cancel the contract, observing a notice period of
one month, within one month of the conclusion of the negotiations on the indemnity.

10.2 Change of the insured premises

Where the policyholder moves the household to other premises, cover passes to those
premises. Both sets of premises are covered during the removal, for a maximum of
[number] months. The change must be notified without delay in text form.

10.3 Change of the rating features

Where a rating feature changes, 6.7 applies. The insurer may cancel the contract
where the policyholder does not agree to a premium adjusted in accordance with 6.7,
observing a notice period of one month.

10.4 Duties of notification

Changes of the kind described in 10.2 and 10.3 must be notified without delay in
text form. Where notification has been omitted, the insurer is not obliged to pay
in the insured event only where the event occurred later than one month after
notification ought to have been received and the insurer demonstrates that it would
not have concluded the existing contract on the changed circumstances.

===============================================================================
END OF DOCUMENT

case.description:
Burglary at the policyholder's home, and a fuller claim on this one. The front door was forced overnight and a range of things were taken from the ground floor and the bedroom - clothing, several pieces of jewellery, and some odds and ends.

Among the clothing was a winter coat that had only been worn a couple of times, and the settlement agent also put in for a premium designer jacket to replace a stolen mid-range one. The jewellery included several everyday unscheduled pieces plus one high-value ring, which this policy carries on a scheduled-articles endorsement. There was also a claim for an antique brooch, though there was no receipt, photo or valuation for it. On top of the property, the agent listed personal mileage to and from the police station and time spent putting the claim together.

A locksmith boarded up and re-keyed the forced door the same night, and also cleaned up the muddy footprints the intruders had tracked through the hallway.

The police attended and there is a crime reference.
